paragraphs.text: Monokai Pro theme for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI — six official filters, syntax highlighting, inst
allable as a DSH plugin bundle.
# Monokai Pro for DSH
**A dark UI/UX theme for the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI, ported from Monokai Pro.**

Official palette values from the Monokai Pro VS Code extension (2.0.16) — not approximated.
Delivere
d as a Cordis bundle with a Client half, so it survives restarts and applies to the running page.
## Highlights
- **Six official filters** — Monokai Pro, Classic, Octagon, Ristretto, Spectrum and Machine, selecta

ble as swatches in the settings row (dark scheme only, exactly like the real product).
- **Warm char
coal surfaces** — `#2D2A2E` workspace, `#221F22` sidebar/status/title, `#19181A` deepest chrome, `#4
03E41` widgets, panels, menus and inputs. Every filter maps its own `background`/`dark1`/`dark2`/`di

mmed5` roles onto these.
- **Monokai text ladder** — `#FCFCFA` primary, `#C1C0C0` secondary, `#93929

3` tertiary, `#727072` captions, `#5B595C` dimmed, each taken from the active filter.
- **Six-color
accent family** — yellow `#FFD866` brand and primary action, pink `#FF6188` errors, orange `#FC9867`

warnings, green `#A9DC76` success, cyan `#78DCE8` info, purple `#AB9DF2` constants.
- **Monokai syn
tax highlighting** — pink keywords, yellow strings, green functions, purple constants, orange parame

ters and grey comments.
- **Complete chrome** — yellow accent wash for active and hover states, them

ed focus rings, scrollbars, toasts, tooltips and diffs.
- **Code-first typography** — Avenir Next →
Inter → Segoe UI Variable Text in the UI, JetBrains Mono → Cascadia Code → Fira Code → SF Mono in co

de. A user font chosen in **Settings → General → Font settings** still wins.
- **Light mode included
** — the official Monokai Pro Light counterpart (`#FAF4F2` canvas, `#EDE7E5` sidebar, `#29242A` text
), so switching Appearance to Light never leaves half-themed surfaces. Filters apply to dark only.
## What is DSH?
DeepSeek Harness (DSH) boots a profile — an ordered stack of plugin-bundle patch layers on top of a
DeepSeek app (web GUI, TUI, headless…). This package is one of those plugin bundles: it carries no H
ost code, only a Client half that injects the theme into the Web GUI.
## Installation
**Requirements**
- A working DSH install (`dsh` on your `PATH`) with a profile that includes the Web GUI, e.g. `web`.
- No build step and no peer dependencies — `client.js` ships as written.
**From npm (recommended)**
[代码示例省略，未执行]
For the default Web GUI profile that is:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
The package is `dsh-monokai-pro` on the npm registry; `dsh plugin … add` delegates to pnpm, so `npm`
/`pnpm` dist-tags and version ranges work the same way.
**From GitHub**
The npm package and this repository are published in lockstep — installing from npm is always the ea
sier path. To hack on the theme instead, clone the repo and install it from the local directory:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
**After installing**
1. Reload the Web page once after installing or updating the bundle, so the browser loads the curren

t `client.js` generation.
2. Open **Settings → General** — the **Monokai Pro** row sits after Transc

ript view.
3. The switch is on by default on first install, and that first activation also sets the
appearance preference to **Dark**. Turning the switch off removes the token layer immediately and le

aves the built-in palette in place.
4. Pick a filter with the swatches under the description: each d
ot previews the variant's canvas (lower-left half) and its pink accent (upper-right half).
**Updating & removal**
[代码示例省略，未执行]
> The switch state and the filter choice are browser-local (`localStorage`, keys `dsh.plugin.monokai
-pro.enabled` and `dsh.plugin.monokai-pro.variant`). The theme service persists only the built-in `l
ight` / `dark` / `system` preference, so a third-party layer cannot store its own id in the Host set
tings document — the palette itself always reapplies on reload.
## How it works
- `client.js` calls `ctx.theme.overrideTokens(packageId, tokens)` — a stacked alias-token layer over
whatever built-in theme is active. Removing the layer restores exactly the tokens it covered; the b

ase palette is never edited.
- `buildTokens(palette)` derives the whole layer from one filter's pale

tte object, so adding a variant is adding twelve hex values, not touching the token map.
- Every val

ue is supplied as a `{ light, dark }` pair, as the theme service requires.
- The row is contributed
to the `settings.general.item` slot and uses only `--dsw-alias-*` tokens plus `role="switch"` / `ari

a-checked` / `aria-pressed` semantics.
- `index.js` is an empty Host half; the bundle exists so the
profile can carry the Client row and the plugin stays visible in the plugin inventory.
Palette reference

The Pro filter below is reverse-engineered from the official Monokai Pro VS
Code extension (`theme-m

onokai-pro-vscode` 2.0.16, `themes/Monokai Pro.json`
and `Monokai Pro Light.json`, kept in this repo

as
`Monokai Pro-reference.json`). The other five filters are transcribed from the
official palettes

as mirrored by `monokai-pro.nvim`
(`lua/monokai-pro/palette/*.lua`), whose Pro and Light entries ma

tch the
extension JSON value-for-value. Every value used by the token layer traces to
one of these h

exes or to an alpha step the reference itself uses — no invented
colors remain in the dark scheme.
| Role               | Pro dark  | Light                      |

| Background deepest | `#19181A` | `#E0DAD9` (activity)       |
| Background deep    | `#221F22` | `

#EDE7E5` (sidebar/status) |
| Background         | `#2D2A2E` | `#FAF4F2`                  |
| Surfac

e            | `#403E41` | `#FEFAF9`                  |
| Border             | `#5B595C` | `#D3CDCC`

|
| Focus              | `#727072` | `#A59FA0`                  |
| Text soft

|
| Text dimmed        | `#727072` | `#BFB9BA`                  |
| Foreground         | `

#FCFCFA` | `#29242A`                  |
